Subject: Orionix renewal: tiered commit swap + upfront credit proposal

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table so your procurement & finance teams have something concrete to review. High-level idea:

- Term: 12 months (renewal effective 2027-01-01)
- Commit swap: move from current 6M token commit/year to a tiered 9M commit with quarterly true-ups
- Upfront credit: Redwood will apply a one-time $75,000 credit against invoices (see mechanics below)
- Price anchor: fixed per-token rate for the first 6 months of the new term (protects you during initial migration)
- Burst capacity: guaranteed burst pool at X throughput with capped overage rates; usage beyond burst billed at standard overage rates

Mechanics we propose: the $75k credit is issued as an invoice credit split over first 3 invoices (to simplify accounting). The tiered commit gives you a lower effective price at 9M+, with stepped rates for 6–9M and 9M+. We can also add a short SLA offset clause for critical incidents during the first 90 days of migration.

I attached a rough pricing_workbook_Q4.xlsx so you can see the modeled invoice impact (it includes amortization of the credit). If you want, we can convert this to a formal order form and DocuSign once we lock numbers.

Next steps: would you be able to confirm the internal approvers and any timeline constraints? If procurement wants an alternate credit amortization (e.g., single upfront invoice vs. three-month split), we can be flexible.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Hi Sophie / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick review and for sending Q3 usage. We ran the numbers and can confirm Redwood is comfortable with the single upfront credit applied to the first invoice. To summarize and confirm next steps so procurement has a single source of truth:

Final commercial terms (summary)
- Term: 12 months starting 2027-01-01
- Commit tiers and rates:
  * 0–6M tokens: $0.0035/token
  * 6M–9M tokens: $0.0029/token
  * 9M+ tokens: $0.0025/token
- Upfront credit: $75,000 applied as a single credit on the first invoice after the new term begins
- Price anchor: committed per-token rates fixed for the first 6 months of the term; thereafter standard tiered rates apply
- Burst: 10% burst pool available monthly at no extra charge; usage beyond burst billed at $0.0040/token (capped)
- SLA offset: we will include a 90-day migration offset clause in the order form (credits calculated based on incident severity and duration, draft attached)

Operational items / next steps
1) I'll share a DocuSign order form (pre-populated with the numbers above) and the SLA draft for legal review — please confirm the signatory on your side and PO timing.
2) Once we have a signed order form, we'll schedule a migration kickoff and confirm expected go-live metrics for capacity.

If you'd like minor adjustments to the burst cap or the credit amount we can continue to iterate, but the above is the version we'd need to take to sales leadership for final approval.

Appreciate the collaboration — look forward to closing this.

Best,
Laura Bennett
